newsitem.title: USA: China, Russian key arms suppliers, CIA report.
newsitem.headline: China, Russian key arms suppliers, CIA report.

text.p: The CIA has found that China and Russia were the world's premier exporters of weapons of mass destruction during the second half of 1996, the Washington Post reported on Wednesday.

The newspaper quoted from a six-page unclassified CIA report prepared for Congress and said the exports from Russia and China helped Iran, India and Pakistan develop ballistic missilies, poison gas weapons, or a capability to make nuclear arms.

The report repeatedly pointed a finger at China and Russia and said that gaining their cooperation will be "key to any future efforts" to stop the proliferation of worrisome arms to rogue nations or provocative regions, the Post said.
The report was completed in June at the direction of the House and Senate intelligence committees and said it reflected a consensus view among government proliferation experts.
The report alleged that India, Syria and Libya, for example, have attempted to obtain equipment related to missile production, but did not say how successful they had been.

The report also highlighted Germany as "the favourite target" for purchases by countries pursuing weapons of mass destruction, but did not say how much equipment had recently been sold by German firms.
